question: Most people rate themselves above average at being fair and considerate. Say you did too. What would you say about your rating?
answer: Most called their own rating accurate, minutes after reading about the very bias. People judge themselves by looking inward and others by what they do. Searching their thoughts, they find no biased motive, since bias works out of sight. Each person is graded on intentions, everyone else on results.
move: Check your fairness by what you did, not by what you meant.
ask: If a stranger watched only my actions this month, what bias might they see that I cannot?

options.label: It's accurate
options.mirror: Like 63% of the students, just told about this bias. From inside, a fair rating feels fair.

options.label: Too flattering
options.mirror: Like about a quarter. You can see the pull in yourself, which most see only in others.

options.label: Too modest
options.mirror: Like 13%. You may be right: some people do sell themselves short.

scene.why: We check ourselves by looking inward and find no bias, because bias works out of sight.

source: Pronin et al., PSPB, 2002; Pronin & Kugler, JESP, 2007
reference: Pronin, Lin & Ross, The bias blind spot: perceptions of bias in self versus others, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin 28 (2002): 369-381; Pronin & Kugler, Valuing thoughts, ignoring behavior, Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 2007
